description.p: Niksnaks-Hosting simplifies the process of creating and managing Minecraft servers on Linux. It removes technical barriers by automating the installation of necessary server files and handling the required Java runtimes for you.

ul.li: Built-in Modrinth browser for easy discovery and mod installation
Integrated Playit support for hosting without manual port forwarding
Graphical interface for viewing performance and editing server properties
Dedicated tools to create and restore server backups
The window has a minimize button on Linux too, next to close
The About window links to the project on GitHub
The web panel no longer zooms in on an iPhone when you tap a text field, and a long server name no longer makes the page wider than a phone screen

description.p: The web panel now fully supports every server:

ul.li: Bedrock servers get the Settings tab too: their picture, their server name and an updater that installs Mojang's newer Bedrock build while keeping worlds, server.properties and the allow list
After the app is updated, an open panel tab reloads itself instead of carrying on with the old page

description.p: The web panel can now look after a Java server, not just run it:

ul.li: A Settings tab on the server page: give the server its picture, the one the app shows and the one Minecraft puts in the multiplayer list, and write its message of the day straight into server.properties

Update a server to a newer Minecraft version from the browser. It makes a full backup first, reinstalls the loader, updates the mods that fit and moves aside the ones that do not, exactly as the app's own updater does

The tab is hidden for a Bedrock server, and a server on another computer can have its picture and message of the day changed but not its version, which has to be installed from the app on that machine

description.p: A web panel, for handing servers to other people:

ul.li: Open Web panel from the main menu and the app hosts a browser control panel on your network. Add users and tick which servers each may control; they get a dashboard, the live console, performance graphs and Modrinth mod install and removal for those servers, and nothing else
The Start button's checks, the performance figures and the mod bookkeeping now live in one place shared by the app and the panel, so both agree on what is installed

description.p: Reset the app, tidier hosts, and servers both computers can see:

ul.li: Reset Niksnaks-Hosting from Settings: deletes every server on this computer with its world, mods and backups, plus the settings, downloaded Java runtimes and cache. Servers on a host are forgotten, not deleted

Removing a host drops its servers from the list instead of leaving them stranded; "Clear all hosts" does that for every host at once and takes the app's login key back where the machine can be reached

A server started by the app on the other computer now shows as running here, streams its log, takes console commands and stops from here. A server created on a host shows up in that machine's own copy of the app too, and renaming, re-picturing or deleting it follows on both ends
Adding a host asks it for its servers straight away, so adopting them needs nothing typed in by hand
The Hosts dialog now checks whether each machine can be reached, and a host that is switched off no longer freezes the window
Quitting stops only the servers on this computer, and no longer shuts down servers on a host
Backups are no longer taken from a world that is still being written to
Fixed the Create Server button doing nothing, or freezing the window, once a computer had been added over SSH
The chosen server icon is applied when installing on a host, and importing a world onto a host is refused with a reason instead of silently dropped
Fixed "start on boot" silently doing nothing on some Windows hosts, and a firewall rule left behind after removing a server there

description.p: Run your servers on another computer:

ul.li: Add a Windows or Linux machine over SSH while creating a server, and install and run the server there
Log in once with a password: the app installs its own key and never stores the password
Servers keep running on that machine after you close the app, through systemd or the Windows task scheduler
If Niksnaks-Hosting is already installed on that machine, its servers can be adopted instead of creating a new one
NeoForge support, including a NeoForge modpack tab
Fixed a crash when choosing "Add another computer" in the create-server window
Fixed removing whitelisted and banned players, and applying settings to a remote Bedrock server
Restoring a Bedrock backup taken on another operating system now installs a server build that runs on this one
A Bedrock server missing its server files says so, and can install them from the properties page
Fixed restoring a Bedrock world backup into the wrong folder
Browse and install CurseForge modpacks from the Files tab, filtered to the server's Minecraft version and loader
Packs install from the author's server build when there is one, so client-only mods are left out
Create a new server from another server's full backup
Import and export Bedrock worlds as .mcworld, and import worlds from a .zip archive
Fixed a crash when importing a world
Choose Java or Bedrock Edition when creating a server
Bedrock servers use Mojang's Dedicated Server build, with their own properties editor
Allow list, worlds, backups and updates all work on Bedrock
Pick a specific Fabric loader or Forge build for the selected Minecraft version
Added offline mode toggle
Fixed world importing bug
Autodelete backups after 30 days
Added java version selection and JVM arguments
Added support for running multiple servers for peak mining and crafting.
Redesigned the Modrinth interface to be more user-friendly.
